stem: If energy (E), velocity (V) and time (T) are chosen as the fundamental quantities, the dimensional formula of surface tension will be:
explanation: Surface tension S = Force / Length = Energy / Area = E / (L²) = E / (V·T)² = [E V⁻² T⁻²].
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 1: Units and Measurements

stem: If E and G respectively denote energy and gravitational constant, then E / G has the dimensions of:
explanation: [E] = [M L² T⁻²] and [G] = [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²]. Therefore [E/G] = [M² L⁻¹ T⁰].
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 1: Units and Measurements

stem: If the velocity of a particle is v = At + Bt², where A and B are constants, then the distance travelled by it between 1 s and 2 s is:
explanation: dx = v dt = (At + Bt²) dt. Integrating from t = 1 to t = 2 gives [A t²/2 + B t³/3]₁² = (3/2)A + (7/3)B.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 2: Motion in a Straight Line

stem: A ball is projected with a velocity 10 m/s at an angle of 60° with the vertical direction. Its speed at the highest point of its trajectory will be:
explanation: Angle with vertical = 60°, so angle with horizontal θ = 30°. Speed at highest point = u cos30° = 10 × (√3/2) = 5√3 m/s.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 3: Motion in a Plane

stem: One end of string of length l is connected to a particle of mass m and the other end is connected to a small peg on a smooth horizontal table. If the particle moves in circle with speed v, the net force on the particle (directed towards center) will be (T represents the tension in the string):
explanation: Tension T in the string provides the necessary centripetal force mv²/l directed towards the centre.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 4: Laws of Motion

stem: A football player is moving southward and suddenly turns eastward with the same speed to avoid an opponent. The force that acts on the player while turning is:
explanation: Initial velocity v_i = −v ĵ (south), final velocity v_f = +v î (east). Change in velocity Δv = v_f − v_i = v î + v ĵ, which points along north-east.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 4: Laws of Motion

stem: A moving block having mass m collides with another stationary block having mass 4m. The lighter block comes to rest after collision. When the initial velocity of the lighter block is v, then the value of coefficient of restitution (e) will be:
explanation: By momentum conservation: mv = 0 + 4m·v₂ ⇒ v₂ = v/4. Coefficient of restitution e = (v₂ − v₁)/(u₁ − u₂) = (v/4 − 0)/(v − 0) = 0.25.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 5: Work, Energy and Power

stem: Two bodies A and B of same mass undergo completely inelastic one-dimensional collision. Body A moves with velocity v₁ while body B is at rest. The ratio of initial kinetic energy to final kinetic energy of the system is:
explanation: By momentum conservation: m v₁ = 2m V ⇒ V = v₁/2. Initial KE = ½ m v₁²; Final KE = ½ (2m)(v₁/2)² = ¼ m v₁². Ratio = 2 : 1.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 5: Work, Energy and Power

stem: A solid cylinder of mass 2 kg and radius 4 cm is rotating about its axis at the rate of 3 rpm. The torque required to stop it after 2π revolutions is:
explanation: I = ½ m R² = ½ × 2 × (0.04)² = 1.6 × 10⁻³ kg m². ω₀ = 3 × 2π/60 = π/10 rad/s. θ = 2π × 2π = 4π² rad. Using τ θ = ½ I ω₀², τ = 2 × 10⁻⁶ N m.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 6: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

stem: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration of the disc about its diameter is:
explanation: I_normal = ½ MR² ⇒ K₁ = R/√2. I_diameter = ¼ MR² ⇒ K₂ = R/2. Therefore K₁ : K₂ = (R/√2) / (R/2) = √2 : 1.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 6: Rotational Motion

topic_name: Variation of g with Altitude & Depth
stem: The acceleration due to gravity at a height 1 km above the earth is the same as at a depth d below the surface of earth. Then:
explanation: For small h and d (≪ R), g(1 − 2h/R) = g(1 − d/R) ⇒ d = 2h = 2 km.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 7: Gravitation

stem: A small sphere of radius r falls from rest in a viscous liquid. As a result, heat is produced due to viscous force. The rate of production of heat when the sphere attains its terminal velocity is proportional to:
explanation: Rate of heat production Power P = F_v · v_T = (6π η r v_T) · v_T ∝ r · v_T². Since terminal velocity v_T ∝ r², P ∝ r · (r²)² = r⁵.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 2, Ch 9: Mechanical Properties of Fluids

stem: A gas is compressed isothermally to half its initial volume. The same gas is compressed separately through an adiabatic process until its volume is again reduced to half. Then:

options.text: Compressing the gas isothermally will require more work to be done
Compressing the gas through adiabatic process will require more work to be done
Compressing the gas isothermally or adiabatically will require the same amount of work
Which of the case requires more work will depend upon the atomicity of the gas

explanation: On a P-V diagram, the adiabatic curve is steeper (slope = −γ P/V) than the isothermal curve. For compression to V/2, the area under the adiabatic curve is larger.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 2, Ch 11: Thermodynamics

stem: Increase in temperature of a gas filled in a container would lead to:
explanation: Average translational kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to absolute temperature (E = 3/2 nRT).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 2, Ch 12: Kinetic Theory

stem: A spring is stretched by 5 cm by a force 10 N. The time period of the oscillations when a mass of 2 kg is suspended by it is:
explanation: Force constant k = F/x = 10 / 0.05 = 200 N/m. Time period T = 2π √(m/k) = 2π √(2/200) = 2π/10 = 0.628 s.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 2, Ch 13: Oscillations

stem: An electric dipole is placed at an angle of 30° with an electric field of intensity 2 × 10⁵ N/C. It experiences a torque equal to 4 N m. Calculate the magnitude of charge on the dipole, if the dipole length is 2 cm:
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 1, Ch 1: Electric Charges and Fields

stem: As the temperature increases, the electrical resistance:

options.text: Increases for both conductors and semiconductors
Decreases for both conductors and semiconductors
Increases for conductors but decreases for semiconductors
Decreases for conductors but increases for semiconductors

explanation: Conductors have a positive temperature coefficient of resistance (α > 0), whereas semiconductors have a negative temperature coefficient (α < 0).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 1, Ch 3: Current Electricity

stem: A square loop ABCD carrying a current i is placed near and coplanar with a long straight conductor XY carrying a current I, the net force on the loop will be:
explanation: When the near side is at distance L/2 and far side at 3L/2, net force F = (μ₀ I i L)/(2π) [1/(L/2) − 1/(3L/2)] = (2 μ₀ I i)/(3π).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 1, Ch 4: Moving Charges and Magnetism

stem: In an ideal transformer, the turns ratio is N_p / N_s = 1 / 2. The ratio V_s : V_p is equal to:
explanation: For an ideal transformer, V_s / V_p = N_s / N_p = 2 / 1.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 1, Ch 7: Alternating Current

stem: For a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in x-direction, which one of the following combination gives the correct possible directions for electric field (E) and magnetic field (B) respectively?
explanation: Direction of propagation is along E × B. (−ĵ + k̂) × (−ĵ − k̂) = 2 î (along +x direction), and E · B = 1 − 1 = 0.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 1, Ch 8: Electromagnetic Waves

stem: Which colour of the light has the longest wavelength?
explanation: In the visible spectrum (VIBGYOR), red light has the longest wavelength (~700 nm) and lowest frequency.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 2, Ch 9: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

stem: The photoelectric threshold wavelength of silver is 3250 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. The velocity of the electron ejected from a silver surface by ultraviolet light of wavelength 2536 × 10⁻¹⁰ m is:
explanation: K_max = hc (1/λ − 1/λ₀) ≈ 1.076 eV. From ½ m v² = K_max, v ≈ 0.6 × 10⁶ m/s (or 6 × 10⁵ m/s).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 2, Ch 11: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

stem: Let T₁ and T₂ be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atoms, respectively. According to the Bohr model of an atom, the ratio T₁ : T₂ is:
explanation: First excited state corresponds to n₁ = 2 and second excited state corresponds to n₂ = 3. Since E_n ∝ 1/n², T₁ : T₂ = n₂² : n₁² = 9 : 4.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 2, Ch 12: Atoms

stem: In a p-n junction diode, change in temperature due to heating:

options.text: Does not affect resistance of p-n junction
Affects the overall V–I characteristics of p-n junction

explanation: Thermal generation of electron-hole pairs changes both forward and reverse saturation currents, thereby affecting the overall V-I characteristics.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 2, Ch 14: Semiconductor Electronics

stem: A screw gauge gives the following readings when used to measure the diameter of a wire: Main scale reading = 0 mm, Circular scale reading = 52 divisions. Given that 1 mm on main scale corresponds to 100 divisions on the circular scale, the diameter of the wire is:
explanation: Least count = 1 mm / 100 = 0.01 mm = 0.001 cm. Diameter = 0 + 52 × 0.001 cm = 0.052 cm.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Laboratory Manual: Screw Gauge

stem: The number of water molecules is maximum in:
explanation: 18 moles of water contains 18 × N_A (18 × 6.022 × 10²³) molecules, which is the largest among the options.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 1: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

stem: Two electrons occupying the same orbital are distinguished by:
explanation: By Pauli’s exclusion principle, two electrons in the same orbital have identical n, l, and m_l values but opposite spin quantum numbers (m_s = +½ and −½).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 2: Structure of Atom

stem: The species, having bond angles of 120° is:
explanation: BCl₃ has sp² hybridization with trigonal planar geometry and no lone pair on boron, giving bond angles of 120°.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure

stem: The bond dissociation energies of X₂, Y₂ and XY are in the ratio of 1 : 0.5 : 1. ΔH for the formation of XY is −200 kJ mol⁻¹. The bond dissociation energy of X₂ will be:
explanation: For ½ X₂ + ½ Y₂ → XY, ΔH = ½ E + ½(0.5 E) − E = −0.25 E = −200 kJ mol⁻¹ ⇒ E = 800 kJ mol⁻¹.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 5: Thermodynamics

stem: The mixture that forms maximum boiling azeotrope is:
explanation: Water + Nitric acid shows negative deviation from Raoult’s law due to strong hydrogen bonding, forming a maximum boiling azeotrope.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 1: Solutions

stem: The pK_b of dimethylamine and pK_a of acetic acid are 3.27 and 4.77 respectively at T(K). The correct option for the pH of dimethylammonium acetate solution is:
explanation: For salt of weak acid and weak base: pH = 7 + ½ (pK_a − pK_b) = 7 + ½ (4.77 − 3.27) = 7 + 0.75 = 7.75.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 6: Equilibrium

stem: At 298 K, the standard electrode potentials of Cu²⁺/Cu, Zn²⁺/Zn, Fe²⁺/Fe and Ag⁺/Ag are 0.34 V, −0.76 V, −0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction cannot occur?
explanation: Ag has a higher reduction potential (+0.80 V) than Cu (+0.34 V), so Ag cannot reduce Cu²⁺ (E°_cell = 0.34 − 0.80 = −0.46 V < 0).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 2: Electrochemistry

stem: For a certain reaction, the rate = k [A]² [B], when the initial concentration of A is tripled keeping concentration of B constant, the initial rate would:

options.text: Increase by a factor of six
Increase by a factor of nine
Increase by a factor of three
Decrease by a factor of nine

explanation: Since rate ∝ [A]², tripling [A] increases the rate by 3² = 9 times.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 3: Chemical Kinetics

stem: Arrange the following elements in increasing order of first ionization enthalpy: Li, Be, B, C, N:
explanation: Be (1s² 2s²) has a completely filled 2s subshell, so its first ionization enthalpy is greater than that of B (1s² 2s² 2p¹). Thus Li < B < Be < C < N.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 3: Classification of Elements and Periodicity

stem: Which of the following hydrides has the lowest boiling point?
explanation: H₂O has anomalously high boiling point due to intermolecular H-bonding; among H₂S, H₂Se, H₂Te, boiling point increases with molar mass, so H₂S is lowest.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, p-Block Elements (Group 16)

stem: Zr (Z = 40) and Hf (Z = 72) have similar atomic and ionic radii because of:
explanation: Poor shielding of 4f electrons causes lanthanoid contraction, making the atomic/ionic radii of 4d (Zr) and 5d (Hf) elements almost identical.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 4: The d- and f-Block Elements

stem: Which of the following complex ions is diamagnetic in nature?
explanation: In [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻, Ni²⁺ (3d⁸) is coordinated to strong-field CN⁻ ligands in a dsp² square planar complex with all 8 electrons paired (0 unpaired electrons).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 5: Coordination Compounds

stem: In Lassaigne’s extract of an organic compound, both nitrogen and sulphur are present, which gives blood red colour with Fe³⁺ due to the formation of:
explanation: When both N and S are present, NaSCN is formed in Lassaigne’s extract, which reacts with Fe³⁺ to form blood-red [Fe(SCN)]²⁺.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 2, Unit 8: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

stem: Which of the following carbocations is expected to be most stable?
explanation: tert-Butyl carbocation (CH₃)₃C⁺ has 9 α-hydrogens for hyperconjugation plus +I effect of three methyl groups, making it the most stable.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 2, Unit 8: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles

stem: Predict the correct intermediate and product in the hydration of propyne (CH₃−C≡CH) in the presence of H₂SO₄ and HgSO₄:
explanation: Kucherov hydration of propyne follows Markovnikov addition to give prop-1-en-2-ol, which tautomerizes to propanone (acetone).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 2, Unit 9: Hydrocarbons

stem: Which of the following biphenyls is optically active?

options.text: 2,2′-Diiodobiphenyl with bulky ortho substituents preventing rotation

explanation: Bulky ortho-substituents on biphenyl hinder rotation around the single bond (atropisomerism), making non-superimposable chiral conformers optically active.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 2, Unit 6: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

stem: RMgX on reaction with CO₂ followed by acidic hydrolysis gives:
explanation: Nucleophilic addition of Grignard reagent (RMgX) to dry ice (CO₂) forms RCOOMgX, which upon hydrolysis yields carboxylic acid RCOOH.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 2, Unit 8: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids

stem: Method by which aniline cannot be prepared is:

options.text: Degradation of benzamide with bromine in alkaline solution
Reduction of nitrobenzene with H₂/Pd in ethanol
Potassium salt of phthalimide treated with chlorobenzene followed by hydrolysis with aqueous NaOH solution
Hydrolysis of phenyl isocyanide with acidic solution

explanation: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis cannot prepare aromatic primary amines (aniline) because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with phthalimide anion.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 2, Unit 9: Amines

stem: Deficiency of which vitamin causes pernicious anaemia?
explanation: Deficiency of Vitamin B₁₂ (Cyanocobalamin) causes pernicious anaemia (RBC deficiency in haemoglobin).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 2, Unit 10: Biomolecules

stem: In qualitative salt analysis, which group reagent is used for the precipitation of Group III cations (Fe³⁺, Al³⁺, Cr³⁺)?

options.text: H₂S gas in presence of dilute HCl

explanation: Group III cations are precipitated as hydroxides using NH₄OH in the presence of NH₄Cl (which suppresses OH⁻ concentration by common ion effect).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Laboratory Manual: Qualitative Salt Analysis

stem: Which one of the following shows isogamy with non-flagellated gametes?
explanation: In Spirogyra, sexual reproduction is isogamous and the gametes are non-flagellated (non-motile) and similar in size.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3: Plant Kingdom

stem: Tricarpellary, syncarpous gynoecium is found in flowers of:
explanation: Flowers of family Liliaceae possess a tricarpellary, syncarpous gynoecium with superior ovary and axile placentation.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants

stem: Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for extracting energy from carbohydrates to form ATP?
explanation: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration and oxidative phosphorylation, producing cellular energy in the form of ATP.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 8: Cell - The Unit of Life

stem: Oxygen is not produced during photosynthesis by:
explanation: Green sulphur bacteria use H₂S instead of H₂O as the hydrogen donor, performing anoxygenic photosynthesis and evolving sulphur rather than O₂.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 11: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants

stem: Respiratory Quotient (RQ) value of tripalmitin is:
explanation: For fats like tripalmitin, 2(C₅₁H₉₈O₆) + 145 O₂ → 102 CO₂ + 98 H₂O. RQ = 102 / 145 = 0.7.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 12: Respiration in Plants

stem: The term used for transfer of pollen grains from anthers of one plant to stigma of a different plant which, during pollination, brings genetically different types of pollen grains to stigma, is:
explanation: Xenogamy is cross-pollination between flowers of two different plants of the same species, bringing genetically distinct pollen to the stigma.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants

stem: If the length of a DNA molecule is 1.1 metres, what will be the approximate number of base pairs?
explanation: Distance between two consecutive base pairs = 0.34 × 10⁻⁹ m. Number of base pairs = 1.1 m / (0.34 × 10⁻⁹ m) ≈ 3.3 × 10⁹ bp.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance

stem: Which of the following microbes is used for commercial production of citric acid?
explanation: Aspergillus niger (a fungus) is used for the commercial production of citric acid.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 8: Microbes in Human Welfare

stem: Upon exposure to UV radiation, DNA stained with ethidium bromide will show:
explanation: Separated DNA fragments stained with ethidium bromide appear as bright orange coloured bands when exposed to UV light.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 9: Biotechnology - Principles and Processes

stem: In the equation GPP − R = NPP, what does R represent?
explanation: Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) minus Respiration losses (R) equals Net Primary Productivity (NPP).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 12: Ecosystem

stem: Metagenesis refers to:

options.text: Occurrence of a drastic change in form during post-embryonic development
Presence of a segmented body and parthenogenetic mode of reproduction
Alternation of generation between asexual and sexual phases of an organism

explanation: In cnidarians like Obelia, polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form polyps sexually; this alternation of generations is called metagenesis.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4: Animal Kingdom

stem: Smooth muscles are:
explanation: Smooth muscle fibres taper at both ends (fusiform), do not show striations (non-striated), and are involuntary in action.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 7: Structural Organisation in Animals

stem: Which one of the following statements is correct, with reference to enzymes?
explanation: A complete catalytically active enzyme (holoenzyme) consists of its protein part (apoenzyme) bound to its non-protein cofactor/coenzyme.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 9: Biomolecules

stem: What is the role of NAD⁺ in cellular respiration?

options.text: It functions as an electron carrier
It is a nucleotide source for ATP synthesis
It is the final electron acceptor for anaerobic respiration

explanation: NAD⁺ acts as a hydrogen and electron carrier during cellular respiration, getting reduced to NADH + H⁺.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 12: Respiration

stem: Tidal Volume and Expiratory Reserve Volume of an athlete is 500 mL and 1000 mL respectively. What will be his Expiratory Capacity if the Residual Volume is 1200 mL?
explanation: Expiratory Capacity (EC) = Tidal Volume (TV) + Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) = 500 mL + 1000 mL = 1500 mL.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 14: Breathing and Exchange of Gases

stem: Which of the following secretes the hormone, relaxin, during the later phase of pregnancy?
explanation: Relaxin is secreted by the ovary (corpus luteum) and placenta during the later phase of pregnancy.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 2: Human Reproduction

stem: Which of the following occurs due to the presence of autosome linked dominant trait?
explanation: Myotonic dystrophy is an autosomal dominant disorder, whereas sickle cell anaemia and thalassemia are autosomal recessive and haemophilia is X-linked recessive.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation

stem: In which blood corpuscles, the HIV undergoes replication and produces progeny viruses?
explanation: HIV enters helper T-lymphocytes (T_H), replicates and produces progeny viruses that attack other helper T-cells, causing progressive immunodeficiency.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 7: Human Health and Disease

stem: Which of the following is not a component of mature human insulin?
explanation: Pro-insulin contains A, B, and C peptides, but the C-peptide is removed during maturation into active insulin.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 10: Biotechnology and its Applications

stem: Which one of the following is not a method of in-situ conservation of biodiversity?
explanation: Botanical gardens, zoological parks, and seed banks are ex-situ (off-site) conservation methods, whereas biosphere reserves, sanctuaries, and sacred groves are in-situ.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 13: Biodiversity and Conservation

stem: A parallel plate air capacitor of capacitance C is connected to a cell of emf V and then disconnected from it. A dielectric slab of dielectric constant K, which can just fill the air gap of the capacitor, is now inserted in it. Which of the following is incorrect?

options.text: The potential difference between the plates decreases K times
The energy stored in the capacitor decreases K times
The change in energy stored is ½ CV² (1/K − 1)
The charge on the capacitor is not conserved

explanation: Since the battery is disconnected before inserting the dielectric slab, the charge Q = CV on the capacitor plates remains conserved.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 1, Ch 2: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance

stem: Which of the following combinations should be selected for better tuning of an L-C-R circuit used for communication?
explanation: For better tuning, the Quality factor Q = (1/R) √(L/C) must be maximum, which requires small R, large L, and small C (R = 15 Ω, L = 3.5 H, C = 30 μF).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 1, Ch 7: Alternating Current

stem: Unpolarised light is incident from air on a plane surface of a material of refractive index μ. At a particular angle of incidence i, it is found that the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other. Which of the following options is correct for this situation?

options.text: Reflected light is polarised with its electric vector parallel to the plane of incidence
Reflected light is polarised with its electric vector perpendicular to the plane of incidence

explanation: At Brewster’s angle (tan i_B = μ), the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular and the reflected light is completely plane-polarized with its electric vector perpendicular to the plane of incidence.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 2, Ch 10: Wave Optics

stem: The work functions of Caesium (Cs), Potassium (K) and Sodium (Na) are 2.14 eV, 2.30 eV and 2.75 eV respectively. If incident electromagnetic radiation has an incident energy of 2.20 eV, which of these photosensitive surfaces may emit photoelectrons?
explanation: Photoelectric emission occurs only when photon energy hν > work function φ₀. Only Caesium (2.14 eV < 2.20 eV) satisfies this condition.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 2, Ch 11: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

stem: When both inputs A and B of a NAND gate are connected together (A = B), the resulting single-input circuit acts as a:
explanation: Output Y = ¬(A · A) = ¬A, so a NAND gate with shorted inputs functions as a NOT gate (inverter).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Physics Part 2, Ch 14: Semiconductor Electronics

stem: A planet has twice the mass and twice the radius of the Earth. If the escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is v_e, then the escape velocity from the surface of that planet is:
explanation: Escape velocity v_e = √(2GM/R). When both M and R are doubled, v_p = √(2G(2M)/(2R)) = √(2GM/R) = v_e.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Physics Part 1, Ch 7: Gravitation

stem: Which of these statements about [Co(CN)₆]³⁻ is true?

options.text: [Co(CN)₆]³⁻ has four unpaired electrons and will be in a low-spin configuration
[Co(CN)₆]³⁻ has no unpaired electrons and will be in a high-spin configuration
[Co(CN)₆]³⁻ has no unpaired electrons and will be in a low-spin configuration
[Co(CN)₆]³⁻ has four unpaired electrons and will be in a high-spin configuration

explanation: Co³⁺ is a 3d⁶ ion, and CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand causing pairing in the t₂g⁶ e_g⁰ low-spin octahedral configuration with zero unpaired electrons.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 5: Coordination Compounds

stem: The rate of a first-order reaction is 0.04 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 10 seconds and 0.03 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 20 seconds after initiation of the reaction. The half-life period of the reaction is:
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 3: Chemical Kinetics

stem: In the electrochemical cell Zn | ZnSO₄(0.01 M) || CuSO₄(1.0 M) | Cu, the emf of this Daniel cell is E₁. When the concentration of ZnSO₄ is changed to 1.0 M and that of CuSO₄ changed to 0.01 M, the emf changes to E₂. Which one of the following is the relationship between E₁ and E₂?
explanation: By Nernst equation, E = E° − (0.059/2) log([Zn²⁺]/[Cu²⁺]). In case 1, log(0.01/1) = −2 so E₁ = E° + 0.059 V. In case 2, log(1/0.01) = +2 so E₂ = E° − 0.059 V. Hence E₁ > E₂.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 2: Electrochemistry

stem: In the reaction of phenol with CHCl₃ and aqueous NaOH at 343 K (Reimer-Tiemann reaction), the electrophile attacking the ring is:
explanation: Dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂) generated from CHCl₃ and strong base (OH⁻) acts as the neutral electrophile in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 2, Unit 7: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

stem: Which of the following diatomic molecular species has only π bonds according to Molecular Orbital Theory?
explanation: Because of s-p mixing in C₂ (12 electrons), the two bonding electron pairs occupy the degenerate π(2p_x)² and π(2p_y)² orbitals, so the double bond in C₂ consists of both π bonds.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure

stem: Which compound is known as Hinsberg’s reagent and is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary amines?
explanation: Benzenesulphonyl chloride (C₆H₅SO₂Cl) is Hinsberg’s reagent; it reacts with 1° amines to give alkali-soluble sulphonamides, with 2° amines to give alkali-insoluble sulphonamides, and does not react with 3° amines.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 2, Unit 9: Amines

stem: The right option for the mass of CO₂ produced by heating 20 g of 20% pure limestone (CaCO₃) is (Atomic mass of Ca = 40):
explanation: Mass of pure CaCO₃ = 20 × (20/100) = 4 g. Since 100 g CaCO₃ gives 44 g CO₂, 4 g CaCO₃ gives (44/100) × 4 = 1.76 g CO₂.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 1: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

stem: Which of the following colligative properties is preferred for determining the molar mass of macromolecules such as proteins and polymers?
explanation: Osmotic pressure is measured around room temperature (preventing protein denaturation) and uses molarity, producing a large measurable pressure even for very dilute solutions.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 1: Solutions

stem: The work done during reversible isothermal expansion of 2 moles of an ideal gas from 10 L to 100 L at 300 K is approximately (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, log 10 = 1):
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part 1, Unit 5: Thermodynamics

stem: In his classic experiments on pea plants, Mendel did not use:
explanation: Mendel studied pod shape (inflated/constricted) and pod colour (green/yellow), not pod length.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation

stem: The coconut water from tender coconut represents:
explanation: Coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm made up of thousands of nuclei, while the surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants

stem: Double fertilization is exhibited by:
explanation: Double fertilization (syngamy + triple fusion) is a unique characteristic event of flowering plants (Angiosperms).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3: Plant Kingdom

stem: Stomata in grass leaf are:
explanation: In grasses (monocots), the guard cells of the stomatal apparatus are dumb-bell shaped.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants

stem: Match the following genes of the Lac operon with their respective products: (i) i gene → Repressor, (ii) z gene → β-galactosidase, (iii) a gene → Transacetylase, (iv) y gene → Permease. Which option is completely correct?

options.text: i → Repressor, z → β-galactosidase, y → Permease, a → Transacetylase
i → Inducer, z → Permease, y → β-galactosidase, a → Transacetylase
i → Repressor, z → Transacetylase, y → β-galactosidase, a → Permease
i → Promoter, z → β-galactosidase, y → Permease, a → Transacetylase

explanation: In the lac operon of E. coli, lac i encodes the repressor protein, lac z encodes β-galactosidase, lac y encodes permease, and lac a encodes transacetylase.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance

stem: Production of cucumber has increased manifold in recent years. Application of which of the following phytohormones has resulted in this improvement as it promotes female flowers?
explanation: Ethylene promotes female flowers in cucumbers, thereby increasing the number of fruits and total yield.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 13: Plant Growth and Development

stem: The reaction centre in Photosystem II (PS II) has an absorption maxima at:
explanation: In PS II, the reaction centre chlorophyll a absorbs maximally at 680 nm and is therefore called P680.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 11: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants

stem: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes takes place during which substage of Prophase I of Meiosis?
explanation: Recombination nodules appear and recombinase-mediated crossing over between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes occurs during Pachytene.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 10: Cell Cycle and Cell Division

stem: What is the correct sequence of steps in the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)?
explanation: Each PCR cycle consists of three sequential steps: (1) Denaturation (~94°C), (2) Primer Annealing (~54°C), and (3) Taq Polymerase Extension (~72°C).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 9: Biotechnology - Principles and Processes

stem: Sliding filament theory can be best explained as:

options.text: Actin and myosin filaments do not shorten but rather slide pass each other
When myofilaments slide pass each other, myosin filaments shorten while actin filaments do not shorten
When myofilaments slide pass each other, actin filaments shorten while myosin filaments do not shorten
Actin and myosin filaments shorten and slide pass each other

explanation: During muscle contraction, thin (actin) filaments slide over thick (myosin) filaments pulled towards the M-line without either filament shortening in length.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 17: Locomotion and Movement

stem: Which of the following is a hormone-releasing Intra Uterine Device (IUD)?
explanation: LNG-20 and Progestasert are hormone-releasing IUDs, whereas Multiload 375 and CuT are copper-releasing IUDs.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3: Reproductive Health

stem: Myelin sheath is produced by:
explanation: Schwann cells form the myelin sheath around axons in the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS), and oligodendrocytes form it in the Central Nervous System (CNS).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 18: Neural Control and Coordination

stem: The contraceptive "Saheli":

options.text: Blocks estrogen receptors in the uterus, preventing eggs from getting implanted
Increases the concentration of estrogen and prevents ovulation in females

explanation: Saheli (centchroman) is a non-steroidal oral contraceptive developed by CDRI Lucknow that selectively modulates estrogen receptors and prevents implantation.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 3: Reproductive Health

stem: Colostrum, the yellowish fluid, secreted by mother during the initial days of lactation is very essential to impart immunity to the newborn infants because it contains:
explanation: Colostrum is rich in maternal IgA antibodies, which provide natural passive immunity to the newborn infant.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 7: Human Health and Disease

stem: In which of the following animals, digestive tract has additional chambers like crop and gizzard?
explanation: Birds (Aves) such as Pavo (peacock), Psittacula (parrot), and Corvus (crow) have crop and gizzard as additional chambers in their digestive tract.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4: Animal Kingdom

stem: In a standard ECG, which wave represents the depolarisation of the ventricles?
explanation: In an Electrocardiogram (ECG), the P-wave represents atrial depolarisation, the QRS complex represents ventricular depolarisation, and the T-wave represents ventricular repolarisation.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15: Body Fluids and Circulation

stem: In a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, the frequency of the recessive allele (q) is 0.4. What is the percentage of heterozygous individuals (2pq) in this population?
explanation: Since p + q = 1 and q = 0.4, p = 0.6. Heterozygous frequency 2pq = 2 × 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.48 = 48%.
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 6: Evolution

stem: A fall in Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) activates the Juxtaglomerular (JG) cells to release:
explanation: A fall in GFR activates the JG cells of the kidney to release renin, which converts angiotensinogen in blood to angiotensin I and further to angiotensin II (RAAS mechanism).
ncert_reference: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 16: Excretory Products and their Elimination
